** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **The external snapshot root can load orphan snapshots that the updater cannot map to a test file.** With `snapshotDir: ../snapshots`, a snapshot file for a deleted test `B` is now loaded by discovery. `merge_snapshots` keeps `B` when an update runs only for active test `A`. `write_merged_to_disk` then evaluates `path_map[&id]` for `B`. The map has no entry for `B`, so the index panics and `test --update-all` aborts. The same panic already occurs for orphan snapshots in the default `__snapshots__` directory on the base revision. This PR extends the existing failure to the external directory. Skip IDs that have no entry in `path_map` before writing, or switch the writer to `path_map.get(&id)` and skip missing IDs. Keep the updates for active tests unchanged.

After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Check snapshot destinations after symlink resolution, not only lexically.** The new check validates only the lexical components of `snapshotDir`. `write_merged_to_disk` then uses the joined path with `exists()`, `create_dir`, and `std::fs::write`, all of which follow symbolic links. If `testDir/snapshots` is a symlink to a directory outside `testDir`, validation accepts it. `--update-all` then writes `-snapshot.yml` files outside `testDir` without an error. This is the boundary the rejection is meant to enforce. The check must confirm that the snapshot destination resolves inside the canonical `testDir`. For a destination that does not exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and check that ancestor. Reject the setting when the resolved location is outside `testDir`. Ordinary snapshot subdirectories that do not exist yet must still be created and written inside `testDir`. If the project intends to accept only lexical containment, state that rule in the error message and documentation instead.

I don't have a project that depends on this layout; I found it while reading the discovery code. The sgconfig reference describes `snapshotDir` as a path relative to `testDir`, and `--update-all` writes to `../snapshots` without complaint, but the next `ast-grep test` doesn't read those files back. If snapshots are only meant to live inside `testDir`, I'm happy to close this, or to change it so that such a setting is rejected with a clear error instead.
I think reporting an error that snapshot should stay inside testdir is better. Appreciate it if you can help that

Thanks, @HerringtonDarkholme. The updated PR rejects `snapshotDir: ../snapshots` before writing any files and reports that the path must name a subdirectory of `testDir`. The CLI tests cover that error and confirm that both the default and a custom subdirectory still work. All 12 tests in the verification suite passed.

AI assistance was used to prepare the patch and regression test.
